raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix repeated prompts missing a saved Mamba prefix-cache checkpoint with EAGLE/MTP.

There are two mismatches:

1. **Lookup:** the coordinator caps the proof scan at the reusable-token limit (`request.num_tokens - 1`). Attention lookup then drops another hash unit for speculative replay. With a 16,000-token prompt and 16-token hashes, this can stop at 15,968 and miss the saved Mamba checkpoint at 15,984. Allowing the scan through token 16,000 lets the existing drop land on 15,984.
2. **Registration:** when only attention groups are marked as draft groups, Mamba partial-tail registration uses its per-group `use_eagle` flag while the scheduler uses the global `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` flag. The saved state and its registered boundary can disagree.

This change gives attention lookup its extra proof margin, bounded by the request's available hashes, in both reconciled and per-group connector lookup. Mamba receives no extra margin because its finder does not drop a unit. Mamba tail registration uses the scheduler's global flag. The returned reusable hit stays within the caller's limit, and the speculative proof drop remains enabled.

### Attribution and related work

Builds on work by Brian Yu, with expanded regression coverage.

Related upstream [PR #53802](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53802) addresses the boundary mismatch by moving checkpoint registration to positions reachable under the existing lookup cap. This patch instead preserves the saved replay checkpoint and corrects the proof-scan cap, and aligns Mamba registration with the global draft setting. This proposes an alternative at the lookup boundary, rather than the checkpoint-placement approach in #53802; the overlap is explicit so maintainers can choose or reconcile the approaches.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and test execution. This draft is for human review; it does not claim the submitter has already reviewed every changed line or personally rerun the tests.

## Test Plan

The regression extends the existing scheduler/cache-manager test file. A newer retention test is also updated: a 128-token resend should recover the saved 96-token checkpoint, rather than codifying the old 64-token fallback. Its checks that both retained Mamba states exist are preserved. It covers both all-group fallback and attention-only draft marking, fine/coarse hashes, aligned/unaligned prompts, repeated/extended prompts, changed proof suffixes, and reusable-token limits in local and connector bookkeeping paths.

To reproduce red/green in an isolated checkout of this PR, using the repository's prepared vLLM test environment:

```bash
suite=(tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_eagle_resume_checkpoint.py
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_hybrid_mamba_retention_mtp_resend_of_aligned_prompt)
# Keep the new tests, but restore only the two runtime files to the tested PR base.
git restore --source=f0fbc98c488b40a07d3b269aeba2bda3c4c3b03b --worktree -- \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest "${suite[@]}" -q --tb=short
# Restore the fix and run exactly the same tests.
git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest "${suite[@]}" -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q --tb=short
```

## Test Result

The tested base is upstream commit `f0fbc98c488b40a07d3b269aeba2bda3c4c3b03b`; head is `c6a1b11096`. Commit metadata was updated after testing; the code and tests are byte-for-byte identical to the tested version. This PR targets `vllm-project/vllm:main`. The results below are for the exact tested base and code, not a fresh run after rebasing onto the latest upstream main. Final-base red/green validation completed successfully in **3m46s** with a **five-minute** walltime limit:

| Check on tested base | Original runtime + final tests | Fixed runtime + same tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused suite plus updated aligned-resend test | **8 failed, 24 passed** (10.41s) | **32 passed** (8.54s) |
| Related cache/scheduler suites | — | **314 passed** (68.24s), including all 32 above |

All four tested files match the Git blobs in the pushed head. The eight failures are cache-length assertions. The other cases protect behavior that should already pass; they are not claimed as eight additional independent bugs.

The first wider-suite run found an existing test from [#54713](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54713) that asserted the old 64-token fallback. Its expected hit and block counts now require the recovered 96-token checkpoint. The final run above includes that update.

Before porting onto fork main, the original three-file patch on the reproduction base `2a02f6efe319c885e3ccbcecde402e0028f9ec1e` produced:

| Check | Original runtime + new tests | Fixed runtime + same tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused suite | **7 failed, 24 passed** | **31 passed** |
| Related cache/scheduler suites | — | **255 passed**, including the focused suite |

The failures are cache-length assertions, not import or collection errors. Seven cases demonstrate the regression; the remaining positive, negative, and boundary cases guard behavior that must continue to work. All applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff and type checks, pass on the final PR files.

### Real-model reproduction

On the original reproduction base, ran real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` weights with BF16, MTP=3, prefix matching at 16 tokens, Mamba align mode, fine-grained caching, eager synchronous execution, one request at a time, and greedy generation of 32 tokens. Both runs compare cold and warm outputs across repeated, extended, and final-token-changed prompts at lengths 16,000 and 16,001.

| Measurement | Original runtime | Fixed runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repeated 16,000-token prompt: cached tokens | **15,120** | **15,984** |
| Prompt tokens recomputed | **880** | **16** |
| Cold/warm output token IDs | **6/6 comparisons equal**, 32 tokens each | **6/6 comparisons equal**, 32 tokens each |
| Job elapsed time | 3:19 (five-minute limit) | 3:18 |

The original runner explicitly required a lost repeated-prompt tail and printed `BUG REPRODUCED`. This isolates the lookup-cap defect; attention-only draft registration is demonstrated by the unit tests. The result is 864 fewer recomputed prompt tokens in this example, not a measured throughput claim.

Raw test logs are retained separately and are not included in this PR.

These are focused cache correctness and small real-model checks. Model-task accuracy, serving throughput, and real distributed KV transfer still need separate qualification.
